title: Cambridge IELTS 20 Academic Listening Test 4 Part 3
description: Thảo luận học thuật về đề tài tâm lý học và nhận thức chuẩn đề thi Cambridge IELTS 20 Test 4 Part 3.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (1)
lines.text: Part

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (2)
lines.text: three.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (3)
lines.text: You will hear two education students discussing an assignment on teaching handwriting to children.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (4)
lines.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 24.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (5)
lines.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 24.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (6)
lines.text: How are you getting on with the assignment on handwriting?

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (7)
lines.text: Not too bad.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (8)
lines.text: You know, I hadn't realized that children benefit in so many ways from learning to write.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (9)
lines.text: It's such an important skill, and yet most people think handwriting is less important than in the past because people hardly ever write by hand these days.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (10)
lines.text: Yes, and all the evidence suggests children should learn to write by hand before they learn to type, not least because it helps their memory.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (11)
lines.text: That's right.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (12)
lines.text: The physical act of writing helps children to remember letters.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (13)
lines.text: That seems pretty obvious when you think about it.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (14)
lines.text: What's less obvious is how it helps develop their concentration they have to sit still and focus on one thing.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (15)
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (16)
lines.text: That aspect of handwriting had never occurred to me before.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (17)
lines.text: Same here.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (18)
lines.text: I'm not sure I understand how it improves children's imagination, though.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (19)
lines.text: Well, there was that study which showed that primary age children generated more ideas when they were writing by hand than using a keyboard.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (20)
lines.text: I would have guessed that would be the case.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (21)
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (22)
lines.text: I'd never associated spatial awareness with handwriting either.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (23)
lines.text: I thought spatial awareness was more to do with knowing where you are in relation to objects or other people.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (24)
lines.text: I thought that too.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (25)
lines.text: But good spatial awareness is essential for writing because you have to space words correctly.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (26)
lines.text: It's not just fine motor skills that improve through writing, as I'd always assumed.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (27)
lines.text: Handwriting is so much harder for children with dyspraxia, who have problems coordinating movement.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (28)
lines.text: It's good there are lots of things you can do in the classroom to help them.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (29)
lines.text: They need so much more support with letter formation you need to play lots of games to help them distinguish letter shapes.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (30)
lines.text: It takes a lot of patience.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (31)
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (32)
lines.text: I like the idea of using one of those pens that lights up if you press too hard.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (33)
lines.text: That seems like a really simple solution.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (34)
lines.text: Yes, absolutely.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (35)
lines.text: I'm not sure there's much you can do about children with dyspraxia writing very slowly.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (36)
lines.text: It's more important to focus on accuracy, and as they get more confident, I think they eventually speed up.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (37)
lines.text: One quite simple thing you can do is to use grid paper.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (38)
lines.text: So they write each letter in a box, and that trains them to space the letters correctly.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (39)
lines.text: Indeed.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (40)
lines.text: That's more important for legibility than trying to get them to write in a straight line.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (41)
lines.text: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 25 to 30.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (42)
lines.text: Now listen and answer questions 25 to 30.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (43)
lines.text: For some children, it might be better to teach them to write on a laptop rather than by hand, like children with dyslexia.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (44)
lines.text: They often really struggle with handwriting and some just give up.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (45)
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (46)
lines.text: It's not as frustrating for them if they get things wrong.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (47)
lines.text: On a keyboard, they can be more willing to have a go.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (48)
lines.text: But I read that developing fluency isn't any faster.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (49)
lines.text: That's right.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (50)
lines.text: Did you read that article on the benefits of teaching print rather than cursive handwriting, where the letters are joined up?

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (51)
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (52)
lines.text: Well, in the past, cursive writing was certainly considered more stylish and educated, but not anymore.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (53)
lines.text: Teachers' attitudes have changed because it's been proved that cursive is more difficult to learn, especially for children with learning difficulties who find joining up letters really challenging.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (54)
lines.text: I agree.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (55)
lines.text: I was always worried that my poor handwriting affected my exam results, and now research shows that I was right to worry.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (56)
lines.text: I'm sure a lot of students think it's unfair that they're being judged on their handwriting, not just their knowledge.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (57)
lines.text: Marks are definitely affected if examiners can't read the script.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (58)
lines.text: That's why it's always been so important to teach children to write legibly.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (59)
lines.text: Do you think the role of handwriting will change in the future?

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (60)
lines.text: I can't see that changing much.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (61)
lines.text: Touch typing still isn't taught in most schools, which is a shame.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (62)
lines.text: But maybe that won't be necessary in the future because people will also be able to write by hand on digital devices.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (63)
lines.text: Anyway, teachers understand the value of handwriting.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (64)
lines.text: It's a basic life skill.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (65)
lines.text: True.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (66)
lines.text: However, the fact is that people are writing by hand less and less and relying on digital devices.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (67)
lines.text: That does cause some problems.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (68)
lines.text: You mean like note taking.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (69)
lines.text: There are lots of apps for that.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (70)
lines.text: And for reading historical documents, apparently.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (71)
lines.text: But my mum is shocked by my awful spelling and the fact that my punctuation is really inconsistent.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (72)
lines.text: I think you can put that down to lack of practice.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (73)
lines.text: I expect so.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (74)
lines.text: Personally, I miss writing by hand.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (75)
lines.text: I hardly ever write anything now.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (76)
lines.text: I remember my grandparents had such beautiful handwriting and it was so individual.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (77)
lines.text: Nobody I know would be able to identify my handwriting now.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (78)
lines.text: It's a shame.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (79)
lines.text: I know.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (80)
lines.text: I feel the same way.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (81)
lines.text: I used to write a diary by hand and now I do that digitally.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (82)
lines.text: It just seems less effort to do it that way.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (83)
lines.text: So it's not just a problem.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (84)
lines.text: That is the end of part three.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (85)
lines.text: You now have thirty seconds to check your answers to part three.
